questions.question: Where should application.properties or application.yml be placed in a Maven Spring Boot project?
options: The project root next to pom.xml
questions.explanation: Spring Boot loads these files from the classpath root, which for Maven is src/main/resources.

questions.question: Both application.properties and application.yml define bakery.daily-limit with different values. Which value does the app use?
options: The larger of the two values
questions.explanation: When both files are in the same location, the properties file has higher priority than the YAML file.

questions.question: application.yml has 'server:' and, indented under it, 'port: 9090'. Which flat key does Spring Boot create from it?
questions.explanation: YAML nesting is flattened with dots, so server with port under it becomes the key server.port.

questions.question: A developer writes 'port:8081' (no space after the colon) in application.yml and the port does not change. What is the bug?
options: YAML needs a space after the colon, otherwise it is plain text
The key must be written in capital letters
The value must be inside double quotes
The file must be named application.yaml
questions.explanation: Without the space, port:8081 is read as one text value, not as a key with a value.

questions.question: An application.yml indents a nested key with a tab character and the app fails to start. What is the fix?
options: Add a semicolon at the end of each line
Move the file to the project root
Use spaces for indentation, never tabs
questions.explanation: YAML forbids tab characters for indentation, so every level must be indented with spaces.
